advances: The proposed four-term scalar bridge fails even on a Cartesian product of two complete one-step supports. Its original mass on points with at most one coordinate equal to two, every single coordinate-two face mass, the scaled Boolean-midpoint kernel, and the scaled fourth-power sum all tend to zero simultaneously. Nevertheless the original third depth moment has a positive absolute lower bound at the required ambient scale on this same family. Thus this is a counterexample to the sufficient scalar bridge, not to the original moment problem or the locked mixed-integer depth statement.

proof:
Apply the initial convex-realization lemma of \(032423921efad6c8\) with all possible one-step extension points included. It gives \(\operatorname{conv}(D^{(1)}_j)\cap\mathbb Z^j=D^{(1)}_j\) for \(j=r,m\). For any finite sets \(F,G\), one has \(\operatorname{conv}(F\times G)=\operatorname{conv}(F)\times\operatorname{conv}(G)\): the forward containment follows by projection, and if \(x=\sum_i a_i f_i\), \(y=\sum_j b_j g_j\) are convex combinations, then \((x,y)=\sum_{i,j}a_i b_j(f_i,g_j)\) is a convex combination in \(F\times G\). Therefore
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{conv}(D)\cap\mathbb Z^{r+m}
&=\bigl(\operatorname{conv}(D^{(1)}_r)\cap\mathbb Z^r\bigr)
\times\bigl(\operatorname{conv}(D^{(1)}_m)\cap\mathbb Z^m\bigr)\\
&=D^{(1)}_r\times D^{(1)}_m=D.
\end{aligned}
$$
The hull contains \([0,1]^k\), so it is full-dimensional in \(\mathbb R^k\). Each factor contains its Boolean cube and has at most one coordinate two per point. This proves all stated support properties. The height-zero embedding \(A\) introduces no new support points or weights.

Put \(q=T^2/(1+T)\), \(h_H=1+rq\), and \(h=1+m/2\). The high-activity block and the uniform block have partition functions
$$
\begin{aligned}
Z_H
&=(1+T)^r+rT^2(1+T)^{r-1}
=(1+T)^r h_H,\\
Z_L&=2^m+m2^{m-1}=2^m h.
\end{aligned}
$$
Indeed, in the high-activity block the Boolean points contribute \((1+T)^r\). Fixing the unique coordinate two gives contribution \(T^2(1+T)^{r-1}\), and there are \(r\) choices. The uniform-block count follows in the same way at activity one. Thus \(Z=Z_H Z_L\), and, on defining
$$
\mu_u=\frac{T^{\sum_i u_i}}{Z_H}
\quad(u\in D^{(1)}_r),
\qquad
\nu_v=\frac1{Z_L}
\quad(v\in D^{(1)}_m),
$$
the original probability is exactly \(p_{(u,v)}=\mu_u\nu_v\). These marginals are the original factors of the given affine law.

The probabilities that the two blocks have a coordinate two are respectively \((h_H-1)/h_H\) and \((h-1)/h\). A product point has two coordinates equal to two precisely when both events occur. Independence therefore gives the exact formula
$$
\alpha=1-\left(1-\frac1{h_H}\right)
\left(1-\frac1h\right)
=\frac1{h_H}+\frac1h-\frac1{h_Hh}.
$$
Since \(T=m\ge1\), one has \(q\ge m/2\), and hence \(m/h_H\le2/r\to0\), whereas \(m/h\to2\). The displayed formula proves \(m\alpha\to2\).

Each high-activity coordinate has coordinate-two mass \(q/h_H\), and each uniform-block coordinate has coordinate-two mass \(1/(m+2)\). These assertions follow by fixing that coordinate two in the respective partition sums. The high-activity mass is larger: \(m\ge r\), \(q\ge m/2\), and
$$
q(m+2-r)\ge m>1
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\frac{q}{1+rq}>\frac1{m+2}.
$$
Consequently \(\max_i p(x_i=2)=q/(1+rq)\), and multiplying by \(r\) gives a limit of one because \(rq\to\infty\). In particular every such face mass tends to zero.

We next compute the entire Boolean-midpoint kernel, including all pairs that use a diagonal in just one block. In a one-step block, a parity class has a Boolean source \(b\) and its extensions \(b+2e_i\) over coordinates with \(b_i=0\). The ordered pairs in that class whose midpoint is Boolean are exactly: the Boolean diagonal \((b,b)\); a Boolean source and one of its extensions, in either order; and two extensions with distinct indices. A repeated extension has a coordinate-two midpoint and is excluded. Different parity classes cannot give an integer midpoint. This is a complete classification.

Put \(U=1+T^{4/3}\). The contribution of Boolean diagonals in the high-activity block is
\(D_H=U^r/Z_H^{4/3}\). Let \(K_H\) be the high-activity kernel over all ordered pairs with Boolean midpoint, including these Boolean diagonals. The classification gives
$$
K_H=\frac{
U^r+2rT^{1/3}U^{r-1}
+r(r-1)T^{8/3}U^{r-2}}
{Z_H^{4/3}}
=D_H C_H,
$$
where
$$
C_H=1+\frac{2rT^{1/3}}U
+\frac{r(r-1)T^{8/3}}{U^2}.
$$
To verify the weighted terms, if \(b\) is Boolean and \(b_i=0\), the probabilities of \(b\) and \(b+2e_i\) are in ratio \(T^2\). Their ordered-pair summand is \(T^{(4/3)\sum b_j+1/3}/Z_H^{4/3}\). Summing the unrestricted \(r-1\) Boolean coordinates and both orientations gives \(2rT^{1/3}U^{r-1}/Z_H^{4/3}\). For distinct indices \(i,j\), both extension probabilities equal \(T^{\sum b_j+2}/Z_H\), with \(b_i=b_j=0\). Summing the other \(r-2\) Boolean coordinates and all \(r(r-1)\) ordered index choices gives \(r(r-1)T^{8/3}U^{r-2}/Z_H^{4/3}\). Thus every term in the formula has the required minimum and maximum endpoint exponents.

In the uniform block, the total number of ordered pairs with Boolean midpoint, again including Boolean diagonals, is \(2^m J\), where \(J=1+(m^2+3m)/4\). Indeed, the three classes in the same classification contain respectively \(2^m\), \(m2^m\), and \(m(m-1)2^{m-2}\) pairs. The last count chooses the ordered distinct extension indices and freely chooses all other Boolean coordinates. Their sum is exactly \(2^m J\).

A product pair has Boolean midpoint exactly when both block pairs do. Moreover, since \(\nu_v\) is constant over its full support, for any such product endpoints the kernel summand is \(Z_L^{-4/3}\) times the high-activity kernel summand. This equality retains the actual smaller endpoint: the relative order of the two original product probabilities depends only on their high-activity probabilities. It does not replace the minimum by a geometric mean.

Before excluding the global diagonal, the product sum is therefore \(Z_L^{-4/3}2^m J K_H\). Its global diagonal pairs with Boolean midpoint are exactly \(((u,v),(u,v))\) with \(u\in B_r\), \(v\in B_m\). Their total is \(Z_L^{-4/3}2^m D_H\). In particular a Boolean diagonal in just one block must remain when the other block endpoints differ. Subtracting only the global diagonal proves the exact identities
$$
\begin{aligned}
L_B&=2^{-m/3}h^{-4/3}D_H(JC_H-1),\\
2^{k/3}L_B&=2^{r/3}h^{-4/3}D_H(JC_H-1).
\end{aligned}
$$

Here \(r/T\to0\), since \(T=4^r\), and \(h_H/(rT)=1/(rT)+T/(1+T)\to1\). Rewriting \(D_H\) gives
$$
D_H(rT)^{4/3}
=\frac{(1+T^{-4/3})^r}{(1+T^{-1})^{4r/3}}
\left(\frac{rT}{h_H}\right)^{4/3}
\longrightarrow1.
$$
For the ratio of powers, the logarithm has absolute value at most \(rT^{-4/3}+(4r/3)T^{-1}\), which tends to zero, using \(0\le\log(1+s)\le s\) for \(s\ge0\). Also \(C_H/r^2\to1\): its first term divided by \(r^2\) tends to zero; its second divided by \(r^2\) is at most \(2/(rT)\); and its third divided by \(r^2\) is
\((1-1/r)(1+T^{-4/3})^{-2}\to1\).
Since \(J/m^2\to1/4\), we obtain \((JC_H-1)/(r^2m^2)\to1/4\). Finally \(2^{r/3}m^{-2/3}=2^{-r}\), so the exact scaled-kernel formula yields
$$
\frac{2^{k/3}L_B}{r^{2/3}2^{-r}}
=\left(\frac mh\right)^{4/3}
\bigl[D_H(rm)^{4/3}\bigr]
\frac{JC_H-1}{r^2m^2}
\longrightarrow\frac{2^{4/3}}4=2^{-2/3}.
$$
In particular this term tends to zero.

For the fourth-power sum, direct partition summation and the original product factorization give
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{u\in D^{(1)}_r}\mu_u^4
&=\frac{(1+T^4)^r+rT^8(1+T^4)^{r-1}}{Z_H^4},\\
S_4&=\left(\sum_u\mu_u^4\right)(2^m h)^{-3},\\
8^kS_4&=\frac{8^r}{h^3}\sum_u\mu_u^4.
\end{aligned}
$$
The maximum high-activity weight is \(T^{r+1}\), attained at exactly \(r\) points, each having one coordinate two and all remaining coordinates one. Write their common probability as \(a=T^{r+1}/Z_H\). The exact normalization implies
$$
ra=\left[
(1+T^{-1})^{r-1}
\left(1+\frac{1+T}{rT^2}\right)
\right]^{-1}\longrightarrow1.
$$
The same elementary logarithm bound just used proves the limit of the first factor, and the second factor tends to one directly. Since \(a\) is the largest atom, \(r a^4\le\sum_u\mu_u^4\le a^3\sum_u\mu_u=a^3\). Thus
$$
(ra)^4\le r^3\sum_u\mu_u^4\le(ra)^3,
\qquad
r^3\sum_u\mu_u^4\longrightarrow1.
$$
It follows that
$$
\frac{8^kS_4}{8^r/(r^3m^3)}
=\left(\frac mh\right)^3
\left(r^3\sum_u\mu_u^4\right)
\longrightarrow8.
$$
Here \(8^r/m^3=8^{-r}\to0\), so the scaled fourth-power term also tends to zero. Together with the preceding three limits, this proves the claimed counterexample to every positive uniform scalar coefficient.

It remains to establish the positive original moment calibration. For a probability \(\eta\) on a finite subset \(F\subset\mathbb R^j\), use \(\tau_\eta(z)\) for its containing-closed-halfspace depth in \(\mathbb R^j\). This depth equals that of its height-zero pushforward on \(F\times\lbrace0\rbrace\subset\mathbb R^{j+1}\). Indeed, the pullback of a containing halfspace \(\lbrace(x,t):a\cdot x+ct\ge b\rbrace\) has a nonzero normal and is a containing base halfspace when \(a\ne0\). When \(a=0\), containment forces \(b\le0\), so the pullback is the whole base space and has mass one, at least the base depth. Conversely every proper base halfspace extends with \(c=0\), proving equality of the two infima. Allowing whole-space halfspaces by convention does not change this argument or its conclusion.

Now take any ambient closed affine halfspace containing \((u,v,0)\in A\), written
$$
H=\lbrace(x,y,t):a\cdot x+b\cdot y+ct\ge s\rbrace,
\qquad s\le a\cdot u+b\cdot v.
$$
If \(a\ne0\), the event \(a\cdot x\ge a\cdot u\) has \(\mu\)-probability at least \(\tau_\mu(u)\). If \(a=0\), use the whole \(x\)-space event, of probability one, which is also at least \(\tau_\mu(u)\). Define the corresponding event in the \(y\)-space using \(b\), with the same whole-space convention when \(b=0\). The Cartesian product of these two events, embedded at height zero, lies in \(H\), because the sum of its two linear forms is at least \(a\cdot u+b\cdot v\ge s\). Under the original law its probability is the product of the two marginal event probabilities. Hence every such \(H\) has probability at least \(\tau_\mu(u)\tau_\nu(v)\), and
$$
\tau_p((u,v,0))\ge\tau_\mu(u)\tau_\nu(v).
$$
This proof includes both zero marginal normals. If both vanish, containment gives \(s\le0\) and all height-zero support lies in \(H\). Thus no ambient containing halfspaces have been omitted.

The distribution \(\mu\), embedded on \(D^{(1)}_r\times\lbrace0\rbrace\), satisfies every hypothesis of accepted fact \(50c34c5bfb703ba9\), with block dimension \(r\) and tilt \((-\log T,\ldots,-\log T)\). The corresponding statement applies to \(\nu\) on \(D^{(1)}_m\times\lbrace0\rbrace\), with block dimension \(m\) and zero tilt. The depth equivalence just proved identifies their moments in those embedded statements with the base moments used here. Consequently
$$
\sum_u\mu_u\tau_\mu(u)^3\ge\frac1{512}8^{-r},
\qquad
\sum_v\nu_v\tau_\nu(v)^3\ge\frac1{512}8^{-m}.
$$
Using the actual original probabilities in the moment average as well as in the halfspace bound yields
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_3(p)
&\ge\sum_{u,v}\mu_u\nu_v
\tau_\mu(u)^3\tau_\nu(v)^3\\
&=\left(\sum_u\mu_u\tau_\mu(u)^3\right)
\left(\sum_v\nu_v\tau_\nu(v)^3\right)\\
&\ge\frac1{512^2}8^{-(r+m)}
=\frac1{32768}8^{-(k+1)}.
\end{aligned}
$$
This proves the stated actual-moment calibration independently of the failed scalar bridge.
statement:
For each positive integer \(j\), put \(B_j=\lbrace0,1\rbrace^j\) and
$$
D^{(1)}_j=\lbrace x\in\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace^j:
\text{at most one coordinate of }x\text{ equals }2\rbrace.
$$
This notation means the complete one-step support, not the chain-domain set called \(D_m\) in accepted fact \(032423921efad6c8\).

For each integer \(r\ge2\), set \(m=4^r\), \(T=m\), \(k=r+m\), \(N=k+1\), and
$$
\begin{aligned}
D&=D^{(1)}_r\times D^{(1)}_m,
& A&=D\times\lbrace0\rbrace\subset\mathbb R^N,\\
w_{(u,v)}&=T^{\sum_{i=1}^r u_i}
=\exp(-\beta\cdot(u,v)),
&\beta&=(\underbrace{-\log T,\ldots,-\log T}_{r},
\underbrace{0,\ldots,0}_{m}),\\
Z&=\sum_{x\in D}w_x,
&p_{(x,0)}&=w_x/Z.
\end{aligned}
$$
Write \(p_x=p_{(x,0)}\) as an alias preserving these original weights and their normalization. Then \(B_k\subseteq D\subseteq\lbrace0,1,2\rbrace^k\), every point of \(D\) has at most two coordinates equal to two, and \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\cap\mathbb Z^k=D\).

Define \(\alpha\) as the original probability mass on points with at most one coordinate equal to two, put \(S_4=\sum_{x\in D}p_x^4\), and put
$$
L_B=\sum_{\substack{x,y\in D,\ x\ne y\\
x\equiv y\pmod2\\(x+y)/2\in B_k}}
\min(p_x,p_y)^{7/6}\max(p_x,p_y)^{1/6}.
$$
The pairs in this definition are ordered. As \(r\to\infty\), the following stronger asymptotics hold:
$$
\begin{aligned}
m\alpha&\longrightarrow2,\\
r\max_{1\le i\le k}p(x_i=2)&\longrightarrow1,\\
\frac{2^{k/3}L_B}{r^{2/3}2^{-r}}&\longrightarrow2^{-2/3},\\
\frac{8^kS_4}{8^r/(r^3m^3)}&\longrightarrow8.
\end{aligned}
$$
Consequently
$$
\alpha+\max_{1\le i\le k}p(x_i=2)+2^{k/3}L_B+8^kS_4
\longrightarrow0,
$$
so no positive absolute lower bound for this sum holds on the specified class.

For \(z\in A\), define the original containing-closed-halfspace depth and moment by
$$
\begin{aligned}
\tau_p(z)&=\inf_{\substack{H\subseteq\mathbb R^N\text{ closed affine halfspace}\\z\in H}}
\sum_{a\in A\cap H}p_a,\\
M_3(p)&=\sum_{z\in A}p_z\tau_p(z)^3.
\end{aligned}
$$
On this same family, one has
$$
M_3(p)\ge\frac1{32768}\,8^{-(k+1)}.
$$
The only predecessor inputs are the initial arbitrary one-step convex-realization lemma in accepted fact \(032423921efad6c8\) and the one-step original affine moment theorem in accepted fact \(50c34c5bfb703ba9\).
